content_of_post_to_comment: I tire of the “the sexes are fundamentally dependent on each other” schtick because it’s only ever deployed against women. Men most certainly do not consider themselves dependent on women in any way, but when women take the same angle, it’s somehow destructive to the very fabric of society. I, personally, don’t buy the narrative. Men and women can exist completely independent of one another. After all, men have treated women as an afterthought for millennia. It turns out the opposite is also true. Spare me the kumbayah bull.
comment: The interesting tension is that independence can be liberating individually while interdependence may still describe how societies reproduce and function. The real question is who gets to define the terms of that dependence.
